examples.title: Indicator Styles
examples.code:
function IndicatorExample() {
  const [style, setStyle] = useState<'dots' | 'circles' | 'lines' | 'bars'>(
    'dots'
  );
  return (
    <Block>
      <Buttons mb="4">
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('dots')}
          color={style === 'dots' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Dots
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('circles')}
          color={style === 'circles' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Circles
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('lines')}
          color={style === 'lines' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Lines
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('bars')}
          color={style === 'bars' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Bars
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Carousel ariaLabel="Indicator styles" indicatorStyle={style}>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="primary" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 1</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="success" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 2</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="danger" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 3</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
      </Carousel>
    </Block>
  );
}

examples.code:
function ControlledExample() {
  const [currentSlide, setCurrentSlide] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Block>
      <Buttons mb="4">
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(0)}
          color={currentSlide === 0 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          1
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(1)}
          color={currentSlide === 1 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          2
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(2)}
          color={currentSlide === 2 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          3
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Carousel
        ariaLabel="Controlled slides"
        value={currentSlide}
        onChange={setCurrentSlide}
        indicator={false}
      >
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="primary" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 1</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="success" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 2</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="danger" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 3</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
      </Carousel>
      <Paragraph mt="2">Current slide: {currentSlide + 1}</Paragraph>
    </Block>
  );
}

accessibility:
- Uses `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`
- Name each carousel for what it shows with `ariaLabel`, such as "Featured products", and leave the word "carousel" out of it, since the role description already says it. Under a visible heading, pass `aria-labelledby` with the heading's id instead, which names it ahead of the `aria-label` the default still sets. The default, "Image carousel", is a placeholder: with the role description it says "carousel" twice, and every carousel left with it has the same name
- Each item is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`, named for its place, such as "2 of 6". An item's own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes the place of that name
- Items out of view are `aria-hidden` and `inert`, so screen readers skip them and nothing in them takes focus. With several in view, every item in view is exposed. The copies a loop adds at each end of the track follow the same rule, so where the view runs past the last item, the copies on screen are the ones exposed
- The track is a polite live region, so what comes into view is announced, except while autoplay is moving it (`aria-live="off"`)
- Autoplay waits while the pointer is over the carousel (with `pauseOnHover`) and while focus is anywhere inside it, on an item, an arrow or an indicator, so nothing moves while someone reads or works it. A browser that leaves focus on an arrow or an indicator a click pressed keeps it waiting until focus moves on. It's a pause, not a stop: once the pointer and focus leave, autoplay goes on
- When the system asks for reduced motion, each step changes the view at once, with no slide, and a step past either end with `repeat` goes straight to the other end. The arrows and indicators change without a transition too. A drag still follows the pointer, since that's the user's own movement
- When something else takes the item holding focus out of view (a swipe, a change of width that changes the count, a new controlled `value`, or the item's removal), focus moves to the first item in view rather than dropping to the page
- Navigation arrows have `aria-label` for screen readers
- The arrows', the indicators' and the items' names are English unless `labels` gives the words in the page's language, and the role descriptions take `aria-roledescription` on the `Carousel` and on each `CarouselItem`
- With `arrowBackground={false}`, an arrow with keyboard focus shows Bulma's focus outline, as a ghost `Button` does, in the overlay look too. With `arrowHover`, an arrow shows while keyboard focus is on it
- Indicators use `role="tablist"` and `role="tab"` semantics, one for each position a step can land on
- At their default sizes the indicators sit at least 24px apart, center to center, the spacing WCAG asks for around a target smaller than 24px, and each mark draws at its own size. The gaps that do it differ by style: `--bulma-carousel-indicator-gap` and `--bulma-carousel-indicator-gap-mobile` default to 24px less the mark's width for the dots, the circles and a phone's bars, to `0.5rem` for the lines and a wider screen's bars, and to `0.375rem` for a phone's lines, which sit further apart than 24px already. A row too long for the carousel wraps, with its rows 24px apart too. A gap you set narrower than its default puts them closer than that
- The indicators take Bulma's look: a resting dot, line or bar is filled in the border color and the current one in the primary color, and a circle is a ring in the border color, filled when current. A resting one falls short of the 3:1 against the page that WCAG asks of a graphic. For that, set `--bulma-carousel-indicator-border-color` to a color such as `var(--bulma-text-weak)` on a class you pass through `className`, with the carousel's class in the selector (`.carousel.my-carousel`, `.bestax-carousel.my-carousel` under the prefixed flavor) so it wins whatever order the stylesheets load in. It draws a ring at each resting indicator's edge, circles included, and leaves the current one, and the dots, lines and bars in the overlay look, as they are. Forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) replaces the fills, so there each indicator shows its ring in the buttons' text color and the current one is filled in it.
- The Left and Right arrow keys move the carousel while focus is on its arrows or indicators, unless Alt, Ctrl or Meta is held, which leaves them to the browser. Inside an item they're left to the item's content, such as a field or a slider. On an indicator they move focus to the indicator beside it and bring its slide into view, as a click on it does
- Previous/Next buttons are disabled at the ends when not repeating. When the one holding focus is disabled, focus moves to the current indicator, or to the other arrow when there are no indicators. When a focused arrow or indicator goes away, as an indicator does when a change of width leaves fewer positions, focus moves to the current indicator, an arrow that works, or the first item in view, rather than dropping to the page
- With `arrowHover`, a disabled arrow hides at rest with the others and shows faded with them under the pointer. It can't take keyboard focus, so focus never shows it
- In forced colors (Windows' contrast themes), a disabled arrow draws in the system's color for a disabled control, at full strength rather than faded, and with `arrowHover` it does so under the pointer
- On a right-to-left page the slides run from right to left. The previous arrow sits on the right, at the start of the line, and the next arrow on the left, and the built-in chevrons flip to match. An `iconPrev` or `iconNext` is drawn as you give it. <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> and a swipe to the right go to the next slide, the way the track moves.
summary: The `Carousel` component provides an image/content slider with navigation arrows and indicators.

parts.summary: The `Carousel` component provides an image/content slider with navigation arrows and indicators.

props.name: value
props.description: Index of the first item in view (controlled); with one item in view, the slide shown. A value between two of the positions a step lands on (see `itemsToScroll`) is shown as given, and the next step goes on from it. With `repeat`, a value past either end wraps around; without it, one that would leave empty space after the last item shows the last full view. Neither correction calls `onChange`. A value that takes the item holding focus out of view moves focus to the first item in view, as a swipe or a change of width does.

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Enable auto-play: one step (`itemsToScroll` items) per `interval`. Without `repeat` it stops at the last position. It waits while the pointer is over the carousel (see `pauseOnHover`) and while focus is anywhere inside it, on an item, an arrow or an indicator, so nothing moves while someone reads or works it. A browser that leaves focus on an arrow or an indicator a click pressed keeps it waiting until focus moves on.

props.name: interval
props.description: Auto-play interval in milliseconds. Default: 5000.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.description: Pause auto-play on hover. Default: true.

props.name: repeat
props.description: Loop back to the first position after the last. Default: true. With several items in view, the view runs on past the last item into the first ones, so it can show the end and the start side by side. Only loops when some item is out of view. Without it, the arrows are disabled at the ends, and focus on the one disabled moves to the current indicator, or to the other arrow when there are no indicators.

props.name: hasDrag
props.description: Enable drag/swipe navigation. Default: true. A swipe moves one step, however far it travels. A swipe toward the start of the line goes on, so on a right-to-left page a swipe right brings the next slide in.

props.name: itemsToShow
props.description: How many items are in view at once, at every width no `itemsToShow<Viewport>` prop covers. Those props read the way a `Column`'s `size<Viewport>` props do: `itemsToShowMobile` applies below Bulma's tablet breakpoint, each of the others from its own breakpoint up, and where several apply the widest one wins. A whole number, rounded down and at least 1. The widths come from the stylesheet, so they are right on the first paint; the arrows, indicators and steps use the count for the window's width once the page has hydrated, and this one until then. With this many children or fewer, every item keeps its share of the width, nothing moves, and no arrows or indicators render.

props.name: itemsToShowMobile
props.description: Items in view at any width below Bulma's tablet breakpoint (769px), fractional ones included. Falls back to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowTablet
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's tablet breakpoint (769px) up, until a wider viewport's prop takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowDesktop
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's desktop breakpoint (1024px) up, until a wider viewport's prop takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShowTablet`, then `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowWidescreen
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's widescreen breakpoint (1216px) up, until `itemsToShowFullhd` takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShowDesktop`, and on down to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowFullhd
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's fullhd breakpoint (1408px) up. Falls back to `itemsToShowWidescreen`, and on down to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToScroll
props.description: How many items one step moves, for an arrow, an arrow key on an arrow, a swipe or an autoplay tick. A whole number, capped at the count in view so a step never skips an item. Without `repeat`, the last step stops at the last full view, so it can be shorter; with `repeat`, the step after the last position goes on to the first one. The indicators mark these positions, one per step rather than one per item. When the count in view changes with the window's width, the first item in view stays in view.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Show navigation arrows. Default: true. They render `type="button"`, so a carousel inside a form is not submitted by moving between slides.

props.name: arrowHover
props.description: Only show arrows on hover. An arrow also shows while keyboard focus is on it.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Show slide indicators. Default: true. There is one for each position a step can land on (see `itemsToScroll`). They render `type="button"`, so a carousel inside a form is not submitted by picking a slide. Left and Right on an indicator move focus to the indicator beside it and bring its slide into view, as a click on it does, mirrored on a right-to-left page.

props.name: indicatorInside
props.description: Puts the indicators over the slides instead of below them, at the edge `indicatorPosition` names. It also turns on the overlay look unless `overlayControls` says otherwise, so on its own it gives the look made for photos: light arrows, and light indicators on a dark gradient band.

props.name: overlayControls
props.description: The overlay look, made for photos. The arrows take the `--bulma-carousel-overlay-arrow-*` colors, and indicators over the slides take the `--bulma-carousel-overlay-indicator-*` colors on a dark gradient band. Indicators below the slides keep their plain colors, since they sit on the page. It follows `indicatorInside` unless you set it, so `overlayControls={false}` puts the indicators over the slides with the plain look, and `overlayControls` alone gives the arrows the overlay look with the indicators below. While it's on, `arrowColor` doesn't apply.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: The edge of the slides `indicatorInside` puts the indicators on. Default: 'bottom'. Without `indicatorInside` they sit below the slides whatever this says, so leave it unset there.

props.name: indicatorStyle
props.description: Indicator style. Default: 'dots'.

props.name: iconPrev
props.description: Icon name for the previous arrow button. On a right-to-left page that button sits on the right and the built-in chevron flips to point there, but an icon you name is drawn as given, so pick one that points the way the page reads.

props.name: iconNext
props.description: Icon name for the next arrow button. On a right-to-left page it sits on the left, and an icon you name is drawn as given, as with `iconPrev`.

props.name: iconLibrary
props.description: Icon library to use.

props.name: iconVariant
props.description: Icon style variant (e.g., 'solid', 'outlined').

props.name: iconSize
props.description: Icon size modifier.

props.name: iconFeatures
props.description: Additional icon modifiers.

props.name: arrowBackground
props.description: Show semi-transparent background on arrow buttons. Set to `false` for icon-only arrows, which show Bulma's focus outline while they have keyboard focus, as a ghost `Button` does.

props.name: arrowColor
props.description: Color theme for navigation arrows. Not applied while the overlay look is on (see `overlayControls`, which `indicatorInside` turns on), whose arrows take `--bulma-carousel-overlay-arrow-color`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: The carousel region's name. Name it for what it shows, such as "Featured products", and leave out the word "carousel", which the region's role description already says. Under a visible heading, `aria-labelledby` with the heading's id names it instead, ahead of the `aria-label` the default still sets. The default is a placeholder that says "carousel" twice with the role description, and is the same on every carousel left with it. Default: 'Image carousel'.

props.name: labels
